findings.description: Critical: Legacy roadmap outcomes use a third identity namespace (`vendor_limit:claude`) that is neither `AgentEntry.name` (`claude-local`) nor `AgentEntry.type` (`claude_code`). The plan correctly rejects provider-only observations that match multiple lanes, but never specifies how dispatch context resolves short names like `claude` into an unambiguous lane `agent_id` before POST `/vendors/{agent_id}/rate-limit-observations`, nor what happens when only the short name is available (404 vs bounded skip vs fail-closed reporting).
findings.resolution: Add an explicit lane-resolution requirement: observation writers MUST carry the selected `AgentEntry.name` from dispatch context; define a deterministic short-name→type→lane map only when unique; otherwise reject/skip without writing multi-lane state; extend the outcome/reporter contract so `vendor_limit:*` cannot be posted as a path id.

findings.description: Critical: D7/spec say roadmap alternates are capability-filtered lanes grouped by `vendor_type`, but `policy.py` / `orchestrator.py` today key `available_vendors`, `preferred_vendor`, and `_STATIC_COST_TIERS` on short names (`claude`, `codex`, …). The plan does not define the collapse rule from lane records → the `list[str]` policy consumes (one lane per type? type strings? short names?), so removing the hardcoded roster will break preferred-vendor matching and static fallback pricing.
findings.resolution: Specify the policy identity contract: either keep short-name policy keys with a documented projection from `vendor_type`/lane, or migrate policy/preferred_vendor/static tiers to `vendor_type`/`agent_id` with an explicit compatibility mapping and tests.

findings.description: Critical: Catalog-only pricing is required, and the catalog-pricing scenario mentions model and token assumptions, but neither design nor contracts define (a) how a lane joins `model_catalog` rows (`AgentEntry.type` vs OpenRouter `vendor` prefixes like `anthropic` vs lane model ids), or (b) the deterministic formula that turns `prompt_usd_per_mtok`/`completion_usd_per_mtok` into the scalar `Callable[[str], float | None]` policy already expects.
findings.resolution: Specify join keys, selected-model or cheapest-eligible fallback, fixed prompt/completion token assumptions, rounding, provenance fields, and `known=false` when no join matches—including how literal `0.0` local catalog prices are treated.

findings.description: Critical: Tasks 3.5–3.6 require dispatcher-result rate-limit reset metadata and ingestion, but work-package write scopes only add a new `vendor_limit_reporter.py` and omit the live producers that already classify capacity (`skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/review_dispatcher.py`, which has both `agent_id` and capacity errors) and `skills/autopilot/scripts/provider_dispatch.py`. The current `vendor_limit:<vendor>:<reason>` grammar also cannot carry `reset_at`/`retry_after`.
findings.resolution: Either expand `wp-bridge-policy` write/verify scopes to the chosen producer(s) and extend the result contract with lane id + reset metadata, or explicitly state that reporters are called only from orchestrator/dispatch context that already knows `agent_id`/reset and list those call sites in scope.

findings.description: Nit: Probe rows expose nullable `stale_after` and D4 treats stale evidence as `unknown`, but no requirement sets the default probe TTL, who writes `stale_after`, or how it relates to `VENDOR_HEALTH_INTERVAL_SECONDS`. Implementers can leave probes forever-fresh or immediately stale.
findings.resolution: SHALL-define a default `stale_after` derivation (e.g., observed_at + N× probe interval), clock source, and read-time transition to `unknown` when exceeded.

findings.description: Nit: OpenAPI accepts both `reset_at` and `retry_after_seconds`, and design calls them optional, but there is no rule for converting retry-after into an absolute reset, precedence when both are present, or whether a limit with neither field remains active forever. Spec expiry only covers “when a stored reset time is reached.”
findings.resolution: Require `reset_at := observed_at + retry_after_seconds` when only retry-after is supplied; define both-present precedence; and define unbounded-limit behavior (reject, default capped TTL, or explicit non-expiring with operator clear).

findings.description: Nit: Vendor Registry OpenAPI documents only `BearerAuth`, while `coordination_bridge._http_request` sends `X-API-Key` and the coordinator already accepts Bearer, `X-Coordinator-API-Key`, and `X-API-Key`. As written, a Bearer-only implementation would fail closed for the planned bridge writers despite D6 claiming API-key auth.
findings.resolution: Document the same multi-scheme API-key auth as existing coordinator routes (or require the bridge to send Authorization Bearer) and add contract/API tests for the schemes the bridge will use.

findings.description: Nit: Design D6 requires bridge helpers to return the repository `{available, result|error}` envelope, but current coordination-bridge operations normalize to `{status, operation, COORDINATOR_AVAILABLE, reason|error|...}` skip/success shapes. Introducing a second envelope for `/vendors` will fork caller conventions.
findings.resolution: Either adapt vendor helpers to the existing bridge operation envelope or specify an adapter that maps that envelope to `{available, result|error}` for registry callers only, with tests locking the chosen shape.

findings.description: Nit: `wp-bridge-policy` write_allow/verification target `skills/tests/coordination-bridge/**`, but the established `test_coordination_bridge.py` suite lives under `skills/coordination-bridge/scripts/tests/` (not writable/verified). `wp-api-producers` also writes `skills/parallel-infrastructure/scripts/vendor_health.py` and its tests yet verification runs only coordinator pytest, so producer regressions can merge green.
findings.resolution: Align write_allow and verification commands with the real test paths (include bridge scripts/tests and vendor_health tests) or relocate tests into the scoped trees before implementation.

findings.description: Nit: Spec scenario “Registry is unavailable” allows the orchestrator to use a bounded injected fallback provider or fail closed, without criteria for choosing either path. That underspecifies coordinator-unavailable behavior for the primary consumer of availability.
findings.resolution: Pick one default (recommend fail closed for availability-sensitive routing, with an explicitly injected test-only fallback) and forbid reconstructing a repository-wide hardcoded roster in either path.

findings.description: Nit: The plan preserves `vendor.unavailable` / `vendor.recovered` transitions but does not require structured logs/metrics for probe persistence failures, rejected ambiguous observations, auth failures on observation writes, or read-time expiry/staleness transitions—leaving the new failure modes hard to detect in production.
findings.resolution: Add SHALL clauses for structured log fields and/or audit/event emission on persist failure, 401/400 observation outcomes, and effective-status changes due to expiry/staleness.

findings.description: FYI: Watchdog today early-returns on the first health pass after seeding `_previous_vendor_state`, emitting no events and persisting nothing. Tasks 3.1–3.2 require first-and-later probe persistence while preserving transition-only events; implementers must persist before that return or first-boot availability stays `unknown` until the second interval.
findings.resolution: Keep the first-probe persistence acceptance test; optionally add a design note that persistence is independent of the transition-event baseline skip.

findings.description: Optional: Design D5 names the path parameter `lane_id` while OpenAPI, DB PK, event schema, and work-package lock keys all use `agent_id`. The dual vocabulary is accurate conceptually but invites mismatched client code.
findings.resolution: Standardize on `agent_id` in design prose (with a one-line note that it is the lane id) or add an OpenAPI alias description making the synonym explicit.

findings.description: Optional: `GET /vendors` has no pagination while projecting catalog costs per configured lane. Current roster size is small, so this is acceptable, but the contract should acknowledge the bound or add a soft cap if agent counts grow.
findings.resolution: Document expected cardinality (agents.yaml scale) or add an optional limit/cursor later; no change required to ship dg-01.

findings.description: Lane identity correctly uses `AgentEntry.name` with `AgentEntry.type` as `vendor_type`, matching `/agents/dispatch-configs` (`agent_id`/`type`), `vendor_health.agent_id`/`vendor_type`, and watchdog transition `entity_id` keys; provider grouping is explicit rather than collapsing local/remote lanes.
findings.resolution: Retain D2; only the legacy short-name and policy projection gaps above need closure.

findings.description: TDD ordering is coherent across design D8, tasks (failing tests before implementation in sections 1–4), and work packages; additive SQL deliberately omits price columns so dg-00 remains the sole pricing store.
findings.resolution: Keep failing-test-first gates; do not add pricing columns in migration 041.

findings.description: Parallel packages `wp-api-producers` and `wp-bridge-policy` both depend only on `wp-registry-core` and use disjoint write scopes (coordinator API/watchdog/vendor_health versus bridge/reporter/orchestrator/policy), so they do not collide on files when run concurrently.
findings.resolution: Keep the producer/consumer split; only expand scopes where missing callers are intentionally owned.

findings.description: Bridge coordinator-unavailable and unauthorized observation-write scenarios are specified as explicit unavailability / fail-closed rejection rather than empty successful registries, which matches existing bridge degrade-to-skipped behavior for other capabilities.
findings.resolution: Preserve these scenarios; align the response envelope with finding 8.
